title: Evaluation of Whether Functional Strength Training Can Enhance Motor Recovery of the Upper Limb After Stroke
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to test the hypothesis that adding functional strength training to UK conventional therapy improves muscle function and walking than either UK conventional therapy alone or increased intensity of UK conventional therapy.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Be between one week and three months after stroke when recruited to the study
* Have some voluntary muscle activity in the paretic upper limb

Exclusion Criteria:

* Obvious unilateral visuospatial neglect
* Upper limb movement deficits attributable to non-stroke pathology
